webgl.title: 3D and graphics
webgl.body: Three.js and React Three Fiber. The web should not be all rectangles — the face you are looking at is the argument.
bullets: The trade-offs of 3D on a phone

design.title: Design systems
design.body: I can draw it myself, and argue with a designer about it. Colour semantics through to glass tiers, one token set all the way down.

ai.title: Building with AI
ai.body: Putting models into real work, not demos. The head you are looking at came out of a single photograph — stylised, then rebuilt in 3D.

ship.title: Shipping beats perfect
ship.body: Ship it, then iterate. One version goes out; the rest is the next version's problem.

oss.title: Open source
oss.body: Whatever can be public sits on GitHub. Small tools written for myself; now and then someone else finds a use.

slow.title: Slowly
slow.body: Write slowly, build slowly, never rush. A light left on is enough.

bentoScrub.name: Step closer
bentoScrub.desc: Scrolling pushes the collage up toward full screen — Flip captures the end state, ScrollTrigger scrubs it, and it reverses whenever you do.

specularEdge.name: Lit glass edge
specularEdge.desc: A feSpecularLighting point light rides the card's hairline rim — the cursor is the torch, the colour is the project's own. Touch and reduced motion get a static rim.

liquidLens.name: Liquid glass lens
liquidLens.desc: HTML-in-Canvas draws the living DOM into a canvas, then a refracting puck magnifies it under the cursor — the link underneath stays clickable and focusable. Browsers without the API get CSS glass.

shatteredGlass.name: Three.js shattered-glass hero
shatteredGlass.desc: Five Voronoi-cut panes with dispersion, iridescence and clearcoat — someone else's experiment; this page just keeps the link.

lightsOn.name: Lights on
lightsOn.desc: The theme switch is opening and closing the gallery: a 1.2s cross-fade wrapped in a View Transition, aurora and imagery changing shift together.

lens.heading: Glass over living DOM
lens.body: This text is still real DOM: selectable, searchable, focusable. The glass is only painted on top of it.
lens.hint: Move your cursor in — the lens follows
lens.fallback: No HTML-in-Canvas in this browser — showing the CSS glass fallback.
